answer.evidence: The spruce trees are drawn in a flat 2D side-scroller / front elevation style. Each foliage tier terminates in a completely straight horizontal bottom edge (rows 24, 36, 46, 58) rather than curving downward to indicate a conical form seen from above, and the base canopy and ground contact show no top-down perspective.

The spruce trees are drawn as flat triangular silhouettes with straight horizontal tier divisions and crenellations (e.g. rows 24, 36, 46) rather than curved contours showing depth from a 3/4 high-angle view. The trunks and base are also rendered in a flat front elevation style.

The trees are drawn in a flat 2D front elevation (side-scroller style): the tree tops come to sharp vertical tips, foliage tiers are separated by flat horizontal lines (rows 24, 36, 47), and the bottom skirt of the foliage forms a completely flat horizontal line (rows 58-59) with no downward curvature or visible top surface from a 45-degree overhead angle.

The trees are drawn in pure front elevation: the apex of each cone reaches the top silhouette, tier dividers (rows 24, 36, 47) and the bottom foliage skirt (rows 58-59) form completely flat horizontal lines with no 3/4 downward curvature or top-down perspective.
